crates/amun-smt/src/node.rs-10-//!    of all leaf keys in the subtree.

crates/amun-constitutional-kernel/src/lib.rs-7-//! This crate provides the minimal deterministic runtime that enforces
crates/amun-constitutional-kernel/src/lib.rs-8-//! constitutional authority during state transitions.  Every operation
crates/amun-constitutional-kernel/src/lib.rs-9-//! that may affect constitutional reality MUST pass through this kernel.

crates/amun-constitutional-kernel/src/lib.rs-11-//! # Design principles
crates/amun-constitutional-kernel/src/lib.rs-12-//! - Capability-gated execution: no action without a valid capability.
crates/amun-constitutional-kernel/src/lib.rs-13-//! - Deterministic state machine: same inputs produce identical outputs.

docs/CANONICAL_SERIALIZATION.md-28-- Maximum `Vec<u8>` length: 16,777,216 bytes (16 MB)
docs/CANONICAL_SERIALIZATION.md-29-- Maximum transitions per witness: 1,000,000

docs/V2_026_ADVERSARIAL_RECONCILIATION.md:20:## Constitutional Rules Validated
docs/V2_026_ADVERSARIAL_RECONCILIATION.md-21-1. A state without a commit certificate is invalid and rejected.
docs/V2_026_ADVERSARIAL_RECONCILIATION.md-22-2. A state with commit certificate but height=0 is invalid and rejected.
docs/V2_026_ADVERSARIAL_RECONCILIATION.md-23-3. A state with higher height but no commit certificate is rejected (height alone is not authority).
docs/V2_026_ADVERSARIAL_RECONCILIATION.md-24-4. Only a state with valid commit certificate and height > current is adopted.
docs/V2_026_ADVERSARIAL_RECONCILIATION.md-25-5. Equal or lower states are never adopted (prevents downgrade).

docs/V2_016G_PARTITION_SAFETY_RECOVERY.md-10-- **Recovery mechanism:** Unconditional reset of `prevoted`, `precommitted`, `seen`, and `proposal` flags on receiving any `sync_status` after rejoin restored consensus liveness.

docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-29-The constructive dimension.

docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-34-- **D2:** Transitivity (composable history)
--
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-42-- **E2:** Closes subtrees (excluded contexts have no legitimate descendants)
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-43-- **E3:** No self-exclusion
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-44-- **E4:** Disjoint with derivability
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-45-
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-46-### Layer 3: Closure (New)
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-47-The decisive dimension.
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-48-Every derivable context must eventually be resolved.
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-49-

docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-51-`∀ C : P₀ ⊢_C C ⇒ Eventually(Excluded(C) ∨ Canonical(C))`
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-52-
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-53-Every derivable context is either excluded from legitimacy
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-54-or becomes part of the canonical chain.
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-55-
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-56-**Axiom C2: Canonical Completeness**
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-57-`∃ C : P₀ ⊢_C C ∧ ¬(P₀ ⇍_C C) ∧ Final(C)`
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-58-

docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md:82:**Constitutional Closure Theorem:**
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-83-
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-84-For any system satisfying D1-D2, E1-E4, and C1-C3, there exists
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-85-exactly one canonical context `Λ` such that:
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-86-- `P₀ ⊢_C Λ`
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-87-- `¬(P₀ ⇍_C Λ)`
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-88-- `Final(Λ)`
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-89-- `∀ C : P₀ ⊢_C C ∧ ¬(P₀ ⇍_C C) ⇒ C = Λ`

docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-114-  old epochs all trigger `⇍_C`.
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-115-- **Closure:** Every proposal is either committed (canonical) or
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-116-  rejected (excluded). No permanent ambiguity exists.

docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-123-1. **Build** (⊢_C)
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-124-2. **Eliminate** (⇍_C)
docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-125-3. **Decide** (Closure)

docs/V7_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_CLOSURE.md-130-The result is a unique, inevitable, canonical authority.

docs/V6_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_RESOLUTION.md-49-### Resolution Rules
docs/V6_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_RESOLUTION.md-50-
docs/V6_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_RESOLUTION.md-51-1. **Epoch Rule:** `π₁` dominates `π₂` if `Epoch(π₁) > Epoch(π₂)`.
docs/V6_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_RESOLUTION.md:52:2. **Evidence Rule:** If epochs are equal, `π₁` dominates `π₂` if
docs/V6_008_CONSTITUTIONAL_RESOLUTION.md:53:   `Evidence(π₁)` is stronger (larger quorum, more valid signatures).

docs/V7_004_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONFLUENCE.md-65-For any context `C`, all maximal reduction sequences from `C`

docs/V7_004_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONFLUENCE.md-152-This is the deepest unification yet:
docs/V7_004_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONFLUENCE.md-153-- Authority is not chosen, not merged, not predetermined.

docs/consensus/constitution.md:1:# AmunChain Consensus Constitution v1.0
docs/consensus/constitution.md-2-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-3-## Preamble
docs/consensus/constitution.md-4-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-5-This document defines the constitutional rules for deterministic consensus execution in AmunChain. All validators MUST adhere to these rules. Deviation constitutes a consensus violation.
docs/consensus/constitution.md-6-
docs/consensus/constitution.md:7:## Article I: Arithmetic Constitution
docs/consensus/constitution.md-8-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-9-### Section 1.1: Fixed-Point Arithmetic
docs/consensus/constitution.md-10-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-11-- SCALE = 1,000,000 (6 decimal digits)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-12-- All values are represented as fixed-point integers
docs/consensus/constitution.md-13-- NO floating point operations in consensus path
docs/consensus/constitution.md-14-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-15-### Section 1.2: Division and Modulo
--
docs/consensus/constitution.md-24-- Legitimacy bounded to [0, SCALE]
docs/consensus/constitution.md-25-- Maximum fixed value: 10,000,000,000 × SCALE
docs/consensus/constitution.md-26-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-27-### Section 1.4: Rounding
docs/consensus/constitution.md-28-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-29-- Banker's rounding (round-half-to-even)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-30-- Used for all float-to-fixed conversions (display only)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-31-
docs/consensus/constitution.md:32:## Article II: State Constitution
docs/consensus/constitution.md-33-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-34-### Section 2.1: State Representation
docs/consensus/constitution.md-35-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-36-- Accounts stored in BTreeMap (deterministic order)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-37-- Each account has: balance, delegation, nonce
docs/consensus/constitution.md-38-- State hash recomputed after each transition
docs/consensus/constitution.md-39-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-40-### Section 2.2: Canonical Serialization
--
docs/consensus/constitution.md-43-- Big-endian byte order
docs/consensus/constitution.md-44-- Sorted keys for all maps
docs/consensus/constitution.md-45-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-46-### Section 2.3: Hashing
docs/consensus/constitution.md-47-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-48-- SHA-256 only
docs/consensus/constitution.md-49-- Canonical byte representation before hashing
docs/consensus/constitution.md-50-
docs/consensus/constitution.md:51:## Article III: Event Ordering Constitution
docs/consensus/constitution.md-52-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-53-### Section 3.1: Canonical Order
docs/consensus/constitution.md-54-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-55-Events MUST be ordered by (in sequence):
docs/consensus/constitution.md-56-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-57-1. block_height (ascending)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-58-2. sender_id (ascending)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-59-3. nonce (ascending)
--
docs/consensus/constitution.md-61-5. event_hash (lexicographic)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-62-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-63-### Section 3.2: Nonce Rules
docs/consensus/constitution.md-64-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-65-- Nonces MUST increment sequentially per sender
docs/consensus/constitution.md-66-- Duplicate nonces are FORBIDDEN
docs/consensus/constitution.md-67-- Nonce validation is MANDATORY
docs/consensus/constitution.md-68-
docs/consensus/constitution.md:69:## Article IV: Execution Constitution
docs/consensus/constitution.md-70-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-71-### Section 4.1: Determinism
docs/consensus/constitution.md-72-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-73-- Same block input => SAME execution outputs
docs/consensus/constitution.md-74-- Outputs include: state_root, receipts_root, trace_root, snapshot_root
docs/consensus/constitution.md-75-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-76-### Section 4.2: Failed Transitions
docs/consensus/constitution.md-77-
--
docs/consensus/constitution.md-80-- Receipt MUST record failure with error code
docs/consensus/constitution.md-81-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-82-### Section 4.3: Receipts
docs/consensus/constitution.md-83-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-84-- Each transition produces a receipt
docs/consensus/constitution.md-85-- Receipts form an accumulator hash (linear chain)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-86-- Receipts include: pre/post state hashes, event hash, success, error code, gas used
docs/consensus/constitution.md-87-
docs/consensus/constitution.md:88:## Article V: Block Constitution
docs/consensus/constitution.md-89-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-90-### Section 5.1: Block Header
docs/consensus/constitution.md-91-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-92-Required fields:
docs/consensus/constitution.md-93-- version (u32)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-94-- height (u64)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-95-- parent_block_hash ([u8; 32])
docs/consensus/constitution.md-96-- state_root ([u8; 32])
--
docs/consensus/constitution.md-101-- timestamp_logical (u64) - NOT wall-clock
docs/consensus/constitution.md-102-- proposer_id (u64)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-103-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-104-### Section 5.2: Block Body
docs/consensus/constitution.md-105-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-106-- Events MUST be canonically ordered
docs/consensus/constitution.md-107-- Block hash = SHA256(header_bytes || body_bytes)
docs/consensus/constitution.md-108-
docs/consensus/constitution.md:109:## Article VI: Validator Constitution
docs/consensus/constitution.md-110-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-111-### Section 6.1: Execution Replay
docs/consensus/constitution.md-112-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-113-- Validators MUST replay every block before voting
docs/consensus/constitution.md-114-- No optimistic acceptance, no trust shortcuts
docs/consensus/constitution.md-115-
docs/consensus/constitution.md-116-### Section 6.2: Vote Requirements
docs/consensus/constitution.md-117-
--

docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-5-
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-6-## Goal
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-7-Bridge the gap between CCS theoretical concepts and AmunChain runtime types
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-8-by creating a dedicated `amun-constitutional-evidence` crate that embodies
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-9-the core constitutional verification function.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-10-
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-11-## Key Deliverables
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-12-
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md:13:### 1. Constitutional Context (`ConstitutionalContext`)
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-14-- Unifies `Epoch`, `ValidatorSet`, and `StateRoot` into a single struct.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-15-- Represents the CCS concept `C = (E, V, H)`.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-16-
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md:17:### 2. Constitutional Evidence (`ConstitutionalEvidence`)
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-18-- Wraps `QuorumCertificate` as the primary evidence type.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-19-- Represents the CCS concept of evidence `E`.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-20-
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-21-### 3. Core Verification Function (`is_evidence_valid_for_context`)
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-22-- Implements the three CCS rules:
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-23-  1. **Epoch Supremacy (Exclusion `⇍_C`)**: Rejects stale evidence.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md:24:  2. **Constitutional Membership (Exclusion `⇍_C`)**: Rejects foreign evidence.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md:25:  3. **Evidence Strength (Comparability `CC`)**: Ensures quorum, preventing conflicting authorities.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-26-- This single function is the runtime embodiment of CCS derivability (`⊢_C`).
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-27-
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-28-## Gap Closure
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-29-This crate closes the semantic gap identified in the constitutional audit:
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md:30:- **Before:** CCS theory spoke of `Context` and `Evidence`, while the runtime used `Epoch`, `ValidatorSet`, and `QC` independently.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-31-- **After:** The runtime has a single, unified entry point (`is_evidence_valid_for_context`) that directly implements the constitutional rules, making the theory executable.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-32-
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-33-## Next Steps
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-34-1. Integrate this crate into the `amun-networking` test suite.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-35-2. Port existing tests (e.g., V3-006A, V3-006C, V3-006D) to use this new module.
docs/PHASE_84_UNIFICATION.md-36-3. Replace ad-hoc evidence checks in `VoteCollector` with calls to this module.
--

docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-1-# AMUN REPLAY PHYSICS v1.0 — CONSTITUTIONAL PROTOCOL FREEZE
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-2-## 1. CANONICAL ENCODING RULES (FROZEN)
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-3-### 1.1 Integer Encoding
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-4-All multibyte integers are **big-endian**. u64 serializes to exactly 8 bytes. u32 serializes to exactly 4 bytes. u16 serializes to exactly 2 bytes.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-5-### 1.2 Hash Encoding
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md:6:All ConstitutionalHash values are raw 32-byte blobs. No length prefix. No type tag. Fixed-width canonical encoding.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-7-### 1.3 Hash Algorithm
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-8-The constitutional hash function is **SHA-256** for protocol v1.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-9-## 2. REPLAY STATE TRANSITION LAW (FROZEN)
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-10-### 2.1 State Root Evolution
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-11-state_root' = SHA-256(state_root || entry_hash || sequence || domain)
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-12-This is the ONLY legal state transition function for protocol v1. No semantic dispatch. No event-type interpretation. Pure cryptographic continuity.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md:13:### 2.2 Ordering Invariant
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-14-sequence numbers MUST be strictly monotonic within a replay session. Any gap (expected_sequence != actual_sequence) SHALL produce ReplayFailure::OrderingViolation.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-15-### 2.3 Determinism Guarantee
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-16-Given identical (state_root, entries), the output state_root' MUST be identical across all platforms, all implementations, all languages.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-17-## 3. TRANSCRIPT HASH LAW (FROZEN)
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-18-### 3.1 Computation
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-19-transcript_hash = SHA-256(entry_hash_0 || entry_hash_1 || ... || entry_hash_n)
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-20-### 3.2 Equivalence
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-21-Two transcripts with identical entry hashes in identical order MUST produce identical transcript hashes.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-22-## 4. EQUIVALENCE SEMANTICS (FROZEN)
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-23-### 4.1 Self-Verification
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-24-execute_and_self_verify() SHALL: 1. Execute trace via DeterministicExecutor, 2. Apply same entries via ReplayState, 3. Compare final roots, 4. Return EquivalenceProof.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-25-## 5. GOLDEN VALUES (FROZEN)
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-26-Golden values are stored in fixtures/replay/ and verified by golden_verification tests. Any deviation indicates protocol violation.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-27-## 6. AMENDMENT PROCESS
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md:28:These laws are FROZEN for protocol v1. Amendment requires: 1. Constitutional amendment proposal, 2. New protocol version identifier, 3. Migration proof for all existing state, 4. Golden value regeneration.
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-29-## 7. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE
docs/protocol/replay_physics_v1.md-30-This document describes the ACTUAL implementation, not an aspirational specification. The implementation IS the constitution for protocol v1.
--

docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-239-## 10. Consensus Rules
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-240-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-241-1. Any block that produces a `constitutional_root` different from the value computed by the majority of validators for the same height and same transactions is invalid.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-242-2. Any difference in `economic_root` (or any of its constituent leaves) leads to a mismatched `constitutional_root`, which leads to a mismatched `AppHash`. This constitutes a consensus failure for the offending node.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-243-3. All roots are calculated in `EndBlock`. No external observer, daemon, or sidecar process is authorized to modify these roots.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-244-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-245-## 11. Protocol Upgrade Rules
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-246-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:247:- `ConstitutionalCommitment.version` is part of the consensus state.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-248-- When upgrading from V1 to V2:
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-249-    - For `Height < UpgradeHeight`: V1 rules apply exclusively.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-250-    - For `Height >= UpgradeHeight`: V2 rules apply exclusively.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-251-- No node is permitted to compute V1 on one height while another node computes V2 on the same height. This constitutes a consensus fork.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-252-- Upgrades are coordinated via the standard protocol upgrade mechanism with a clearly specified `UpgradeHeight`.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-253-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:254:## 12. Consensus Invariants
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-255-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-256-The following invariants must hold at the end of every `EndBlock` execution. Failure of any invariant results in immediate block validation failure before `Commit`.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-257-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:258:**Invariant 1:** `constitutional_root == BLAKE3("AMUN_CONSTITUTIONAL_ROOT_V1" || identity_root || evidence_root || governance_root || economic_root)`
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-259-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:260:**Invariant 2:** `constitutional_commitment_root == BLAKE3("AMUN_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMMITMENT_V1" || CanonicalSerialization(ConstitutionalCommitment))`
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-261-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:262:**Invariant 3:** `state_root` must include `constitutional_commitment_root` as a leaf in its Merkle tree computation.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-263-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:264:**Invariant 4:** The `AppHash` MUST commit to `state_root`. For CCA v1.0, this is defined as `AppHash = state_root`. Future versions may introduce additional roots (such as `execution_root` or `receipt_root`) into the `AppHash` computation, in which case the invariant will be updated to reflect the new hash composition while preserving the requirement that `state_root` remains a committed input.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-265-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:266:**Invariant 5:** Given identical state transition inputs (same genesis, same transactions up to height N), all validators must compute identical values for all roots defined in this specification.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-267-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-268-Any invariant violation triggers an immediate `BlockValidationFailure`, preventing the block from being committed. This ensures that no invalid state can ever become part of the canonical chain.
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-269-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-270-## 13. EconomicTree Self-Consistency
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-271-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-272-Before finalizing `economic_root` in `EndBlock`, the following mandatory check is performed:

docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-301-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-302-The development roadmap beyond the initial feature-complete milestone is organized into named architectural phases:
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-303-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-304-| Phase | Name | Scope |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-305-|:---|:---|:---|
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-306-| I | Sovereign Kernel | Core consensus engine, validator identity, basic governance |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-307-| II | Consensus Hardening | Slashing framework, evidence system, recovery and snapshots |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:308:| III | Constitutional Security | Constitutional proof system, identity and evidence roots |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-309-| IV | Economic Sovereignty | Tokenomics engine, economic ledger, reward distribution |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md:310:| V | Constitutional Consensus Architecture | CCA v1.0 specification, root commitment, Merkle proofs |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-311-| VI | Mainnet Readiness & External Audit | Audit package publication, cross-node verification, stress testing |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-312-| VII | Public Mainnet Launch | Genesis ceremony, validator onboarding, public network launch |
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-313-
docs/protocol/CCA_v1.0_Constitutional_Consensus_Architecture.md-314-The current phase (V) represents the transition from a network that possesses constitutional and economic features to a protocol where the economy and constitution are cryptographically committed to consensus in every block. docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md:28:### Layer 1: Constitutional Possibility Graph (G)
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-29-`G = (V, E)` is a directed graph where:
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-30-- `V`: All contexts that could possibly be reached.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-31-- `E`: All transitions that are constitutionally valid at the time
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-32-  they are proposed.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-33-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-34-`G` may contain forks, branches, and temporary ambiguities.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-35-It represents **what is possible**.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-36-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md:37:### Layer 2: Constitutional Authority Chain (Λ)
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-38-`Λ ⊂ G` is a **directed path** from `P₀` to the current canonical
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-39-context.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-40-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-41-`Λ` contains exactly one path. It represents **what is chosen**.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-42-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-43----
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-44-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-45-## 2. The Canonicalization Function
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-46-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-47-`Canonicalize : G → Λ`
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-48-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-49-This function selects, from all possible paths in `G`, a single
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-50-path that becomes the constitutional authority chain.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-51-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-52-`Canonicalize` is:
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-53-- **Deterministic:** For a given `G`, `Λ` is uniquely determined.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md:54:- **Constitutional:** The selection follows the rules of the
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-55-  constitutional context (quorum, epoch, validator set).
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-56-- **Monotonic:** Once a context enters `Λ`, it cannot be removed.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-57-- **Conservative:** `Λ` always begins at `P₀`.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-58-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-59----
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-60-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-61-## 3. Central Definition
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-62-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md:63:**Constitutional Authority** is the canonical path `Λ` selected by
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-64-the constitutional rules from the possibility graph `G`.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-65-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-66-`Authority = Canonicalize(G)`
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-67-

docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-73-`∃! P₀ ∈ V(G)` with in-degree 0.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-74-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md:75:### Axiom 2: Constitutional Determinism (Final Form)
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-76-`∀ G : ∃! Λ = Canonicalize(G)`
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-77-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-78-For any constitutional possibility graph, there exists exactly one
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-79-canonical authority chain.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-80-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-81-### Axiom 3: Path Conservation
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-82-`Λ ⊆ G` and `Λ` begins at `P₀`.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-83-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-84-Every canonical context is reachable from genesis.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-85-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md:86:### Axiom 4: Constitutional Monotonicity
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-87-If `Λₜ` is the canonical chain at time `t`, and `Λₜ₊₁` at time `t+1`,
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-88-then `Λₜ` is a prefix of `Λₜ₊₁`.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-89-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-90-`Λₜ ⊑ Λₜ₊₁`
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-91-
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-92-Canonical history only grows; it never regresses.
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-93-

docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-103-### 5.2 Conflicting Proposals
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-104-Multiple conflicting proposals may exist in `G`. But only one can
docs/V6_003_CANONICALIZATION.md-105-enter `Λ`. The others are valid possibilities that were not chosen.

docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-137-## 7. Experimental Consistency
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-138-
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-139-In AmunChain, comparability is achieved through:
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-140-- **Epoch ordering:** If A and B are in different epochs, the
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-141-  higher-epoch context derives from the lower.
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md:142:- **Evidence strength:** If A and B conflict, the one with stronger
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-143-  QC evidence dominates.
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-144-- **Validator succession:** Validator set changes are derivability
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-145-  steps.
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-146-
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-147-All AmunChain mechanisms that prevent permanent plurality are
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-148-instances of constitutional comparability.
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-149-
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-150----
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-151-
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-152-## 8. Conclusion
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-153-
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md:154:CCS is a theory of **Constitutional Comparability.**
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-155-
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-156-The constitution does not forbid plurality by decree.
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-157-It makes it unsustainable by requiring that all authorities
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-158-be comparable.
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-159-
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-160-And in a system where comparability is required, finality and
docs/V8_002_CONSTITUTIONAL_COMPARABILITY.md-161-uniqueness are inevitable.
--

docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-2-## Core Specification v1.1 – Final Foundational Axioms
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-3-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-4-**Date:** 2026-05-31
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-5-**Status:** Theory Nucleus – Independent Foundational Axioms
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-6-

--
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-17-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-18-This specification defines CCS without reference to any specific
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-19-implementation, consensus protocol, or cryptographic primitive.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-20-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-21----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-22-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-23-## 2. Ontology (What Exists)
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-24-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:25:### 2.1 Constitutional Context
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-26-A **constitutional context** `C` is the fundamental entity of CCS.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-27-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-28-`C = (E, V, H)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-29-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-30-where:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-31-- `E` (Epoch): A totally ordered value representing constitutional time.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-32-- `V` (Validator Set): A finite set of participants authorized to produce evidence.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-33-- `H` (Finalized State Hash): A cryptographic commitment to the current state.
--
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-35-The set of all constitutional contexts is denoted `ℂ`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-36-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-37-### 2.2 Authority Object
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-38-An **authority object** `A` encapsulates the right to authorize state
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-39-transitions within a constitutional context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-40-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-41-`A = (E, V, Q, H)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-42-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:43:where `E`, `V`, `H` are as defined in the context, and `Q` (Quorum Evidence)
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-44-is a verifiable proof that at least a threshold number of members of `V` have
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-45-witnessed and attested to `H`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-46-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-47-The function `Authority : ℂ → A` maps each valid constitutional context
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-48-to its unique authority object. Authority is now **derived entirely** from
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-49-the context, eliminating any circularity in its definition.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-50-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:51:### 2.3 Constitutional Evidence
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:52:**Constitutional evidence** is a verifiable proof that:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-53-1. A specific set of validators `V` has attested to a state `H`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-54-2. The attestation was produced within epoch `E`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-55-3. The attestation meets the quorum threshold defined for `V`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-56-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:57:Evidence is the mechanism through which consensus contributes to CCS,
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-58-but it does not constitute authority in itself.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-59-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:60:### 2.4 Constitutional Transition
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-61-A **constitutional transition** `τ : C₁ → C₂` is a morphism that maps one
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-62-constitutional context to another. A transition is legitimate iff it is
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-63-justified by constitutional evidence:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-64-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-65-`∃ evidence : Justifies(evidence, τ)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-66-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-67----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-68-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-69-## 3. Axioms (Foundational Assumptions of the Theory)
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-70-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-71-### Axiom 1: Context Dominance
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:72:`∀ Q, C : ValidEvidence(Q) ⇏ Authority(Q, C)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-73-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-74-Cryptographic validity of evidence is necessary but not sufficient for
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-75-authority. Authority requires a valid constitutional context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-76-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md:77:### Axiom 2: Constitutional Determinism (Foundational Axiom)
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-78-`∀ C : ValidContext(C) ⇒ ∃! A = Authority(C)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-79-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-80-For every valid constitutional context, there exists exactly one authority
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-81-object. Authority is not selected from alternatives; it is uniquely
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-82-determined by the context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-83-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.1.md-84-**This is the foundational axiom of CCS, not a proven theorem.**

docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:1:# Constitutional Computational Systems (CCS)
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-2-## Core Specification v1.0
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-3-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-4-**Date:** 2026-05-31
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-5-**Status:** Theory Nucleus – Independent of AmunChain
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-6-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-7----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-8-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-9-## 1. Purpose and Scope
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-10-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:11:This document defines the core mathematical framework of Constitutional
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-12-Computational Systems (CCS). CCS is a theory of computational authority.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-13-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-14-A CCS is a distributed system in which the authority to perform state
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-15-transitions is not derived from consensus alone, but from a deterministic
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-16-function of a **constitutional context**. Consensus serves as a mechanism
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-17-to produce verifiable **evidence** of that context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-18-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-19-This specification defines CCS without reference to any specific
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-20-implementation, consensus protocol, or cryptographic primitive.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-21-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-22----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-23-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-24-## 2. Ontology (What Exists)
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-25-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:26:### 2.1 Constitutional Context
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-27-A **constitutional context** `C` is the fundamental entity of CCS.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-28-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-29-`C = (E, V, H, A)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-30-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-31-where:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-32-- `E` (Epoch): A totally ordered value representing constitutional time.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-33-- `V` (Validator Set): A finite set of participants authorized to produce evidence.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-34-- `H` (Finalized State Hash): A cryptographic commitment to the current state.
--
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-39-### 2.2 Authority Object
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-40-An **authority object** `A` encapsulates the right to authorize state
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-41-transitions within a constitutional context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-42-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-43-`A = (E, V, Q, H)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-44-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-45-where:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-46-- `E`, `V`, `H` are as defined in the context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:47:- `Q` (Quorum Evidence): A verifiable proof that at least a threshold number
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-48-  of members of `V` have witnessed and attested to `H`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-49-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-50-The function `Authority : ℂ → A` maps each valid constitutional context
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-51-to its unique authority object.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-52-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:53:### 2.3 Constitutional Evidence
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:54:**Constitutional evidence** `E` is a verifiable proof that:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-55-1. A specific set of validators `V` has attested to a state `H`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-56-2. The attestation was produced within epoch `E`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-57-3. The attestation meets the quorum threshold defined for `V`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-58-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:59:Evidence is the mechanism through which consensus contributes to CCS,
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-60-but it does not constitute authority in itself.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-61-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:62:### 2.4 Constitutional Transition
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-63-A **constitutional transition** `τ : C₁ → C₂` is a morphism that maps one
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-64-constitutional context to another. A transition is legitimate iff it is
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-65-justified by constitutional evidence:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-66-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-67-`∃ evidence : Justifies(evidence, τ)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-68-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-69----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-70-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-71-## 3. Axioms
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-72-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-73-### Axiom 1: Context Dominance
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:74:`∀ Q, C : ValidEvidence(Q) ⇏ Authority(Q, C)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-75-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-76-Cryptographic validity of evidence is necessary but not sufficient for
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-77-authority. Authority requires a valid constitutional context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-78-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:79:### Axiom 2: Constitutional Determinism
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-80-`∀ C : ValidContext(C) ⇒ ∃! A = Authority(C)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-81-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-82-For every valid constitutional context, there exists exactly one authority
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-83-object. Authority is not selected from alternatives; it is determined.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-84-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-85-### Axiom 3: Authority Uniqueness
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-86-`∀ C : ¬∃ A₁, A₂ : A₁ ≠ A₂ ∧ Legitimate(A₁, C) ∧ Legitimate(A₂, C)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-87-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-88-Within the same constitutional context, at most one authority can be
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-89-legitimate. Dual authority is impossible by construction.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-90-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:91:### Axiom 4: Constitutional Recoverability
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:92:`∃ F : F(Evidence, Context) = Authority`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-93-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-94-Authority can be reconstructed from constitutional evidence and context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-95-It is not stored locally; it is derived.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-96-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-97----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-98-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-99-## 4. Dynamics (How the System Evolves)
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-100-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:101:### 4.1 Constitutional Context Validity
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-102-A context `C = (E, V, H, A)` is valid iff:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-103-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:104:`ValidContext(C) iff ValidEpoch(E) ∧ ValidValidatorSet(V) ∧ ValidEvidence(Q) ∧ ConsistentState(H)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-105-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-106-where:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-107-- `ValidEpoch(E)`: `E` is the successor of a previously valid epoch.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-108-- `ValidValidatorSet(V)`: `V` is a non-empty finite set.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:109:- `ValidEvidence(Q)`: `Q` meets the quorum threshold for `V`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-110-- `ConsistentState(H)`: `H` is a fixed point of the state transition
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-111-  function authorized by `A`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-112-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-113-### 4.2 Legitimacy
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-114-A claimed authority `A` is **legitimate** in context `C` iff:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-115-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-116-`Legitimate(A, C) iff A = Authority(C) ∧ ValidContext(C)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-117-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-118-Legitimacy is not a matter of voting. It is a matter of identity with the
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-119-canonical authority determined by the context.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-120-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:121:### 4.3 Constitutional Transition Rules
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-122-The following are legitimate constitutional transitions:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-123-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-124-1. **Epoch Transition:** `C₁ → C₂` where `Epoch(C₂) > Epoch(C₁)` and
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-125-   evidence for `C₂` is attested by `ValidatorSet(C₁)`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-126-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-127-2. **Validator Set Amendment:** `C₁ → C₂` where `ValidatorSet(C₂) ≠ ValidatorSet(C₁)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-128-   and the amendment is attested by `ValidatorSet(C₁)`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-129-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-130-3. **State Advancement:** `C₁ → C₂` where `StateHash(C₂) ≠ StateHash(C₁)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-131-   and `StateHash(C₂)` is attested by `ValidatorSet(C₁)`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-132-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-133-4. **Authority Recovery:** `C₁ → C₁` (identity morphism) where evidence
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-134-   exists to reconstruct `Authority(C₁)`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-135-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:136:### 4.4 Constitutional Monotonicity
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-137-`C₁ → C₂ ⇒ Authority(C₁) ≤ Authority(C₂)`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-138-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:139:Constitutional authority does not regress across legitimate transitions.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-140-The ordering `≤` reflects epoch ordering and state advancement.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-141-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:142:### 4.5 Constitutional Conservation
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-143-For every legitimate transition `τ : C₁ → C₂`, there exists a conserved
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:144:quantity: **Constitutional Continuity**.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-145-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-146-Every legitimate context must be reachable from the initial constitutional
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-147-context `C₀` through a finite chain of legitimate transitions.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-148-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-149-`∃ C₀, τ₁, ..., τₙ : C₀ → ... → Cₙ = C`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-150-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:151:Constitutional authority cannot appear spontaneously; it must have a
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-152-traceable constitutional origin.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-153-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-154----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-155-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-156-## 5. The Central Theorem
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-157-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:158:**Constitutional Authority Uniqueness Theorem:**
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-159-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-160-For any valid constitutional context `C`, there exists exactly one legitimate
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-161-authority `A = Authority(C)`, and all other claimed authorities are illegitimate
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-162-with respect to `C`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-163-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-164-`∀ C : ValidContext(C) ⇒ (∃! A = Authority(C) ∧ ∀ A' ≠ A : ¬Legitimate(A', C))`
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-165-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-166----
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-167-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-168-## 6. Relationship to Instantiations
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-169-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-170-This specification defines CCS independently of any particular system.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-171-A CCS-compliant system is one that:
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-172-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:173:1. Provides concrete implementations of `Context`, `Authority`, `Evidence`,
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-174-   and `Transition`.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-175-2. Satisfies all four axioms and the theorem.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md:176:3. Maintains Constitutional Monotonicity and Constitutional Conservation.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-177-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-178-One such instantiation is the AmunChain protocol, which implements CCS using
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-179-BLS signatures for evidence, a round-based BFT algorithm for consensus, and
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-180-epoch-based validator set management for constitutional transitions.
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-181-
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-182-Other instantiations are possible and may use different cryptographic
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-183-primitives, consensus algorithms, or governance mechanisms, provided they
docs/CCS_Core_Specification_v1.0.md-184-satisfy the CCS axioms.
--

docs/constitutional/topology.md-6-### Definition

docs/constitutional/topology.md-8-
docs/constitutional/topology.md-9-### Properties
docs/constitutional/topology.md-10-- **Topology-centric**: Different nodes with identical authority dependencies produce the SAME `authority_root`
docs/constitutional/topology.md-11-- **Pure constraint hash**: Excludes node identity, includes only authority relationships
docs/constitutional/topology.md-12-- **Deterministic**: Canonical encoding + sorted dependencies prevents ordering attacks
docs/constitutional/topology.md-13-
docs/constitutional/topology.md:14:### Constitutional Meaning
docs/constitutional/topology.md:15:- `authority_root == origin_root` → Constitutional topology unchanged
docs/constitutional/topology.md-16-- `authority_root != origin_root` but `origin_present` → Shadowing
docs/constitutional/topology.md-17-- `origin_present == false` → Suffocation
docs/constitutional/topology.md-18-
docs/constitutional/topology.md-19-## 2. Lineage Root (`lineage_root`)
docs/constitutional/topology.md-20-
docs/constitutional/topology.md-21-### Definition
docs/constitutional/topology.md-22-A cryptographic commitment representing the **interpretive derivation chain**: `lineage = blake3(parent_lineage || semantic_root)`
docs/constitutional/topology.md-23-
